source_evidence: Lenders consider leveraged loans to have an above-average risk that the borrower will be unable to pay back the loan (also known as the risk of default).
question: Misconception: Because leveraged loans generally pay higher interest rates, a fund investing in them cannot lose money from borrower defaults. What is the correction?
answer: Higher interest rates do not eliminate default risk. Borrowers may be unable to repay, and a fund can lose money; even collateral may not be sufficient to repay the lender.
